target.description: Predict each original participant’s single-trial fMRI voxel responses to THINGS images from the source image-wise 66-dimensional behavioural embedding. Retain the related Figure 6 category-versus-dimension attribution as a separate source analysis, not a substitute primary score.

dataset.description: THINGS-fMRI, article-linked OpenNeuro ds004192 version 1.0.5 and Figshare collection 6161151, with published single-trial estimates, noise ceilings and image-wise dimension files. Exact artifact hashes and row-order/session alignment have not been admitted.

cohort.description: All three source participants, each viewing 8,740 unique images from 720 object categories over 12 sessions; participant-specific voxels and original inclusion masks must be retained.

split.description: Original leave-one-session-out 12-fold protocol. Author code uses unshuffled 12-fold KFold over ordered rows; exact session-to-row correspondence must be verified before declaring equivalence. The legacy five-fold image-family/category partition is an extension.

inputs.description: Source image-wise 66 predicted behavioural dimensions and training-fold response estimates; category labels and the 30 diagnostic dimensions belong to the separately specified variance-partition comparator. Test response estimates remain scoring-only.

preprocessing.description: Author fit joins image names and z-scores dimension columns globally before ordinary least squares with intercept. Preserve source single-trial estimate and noise-ceiling conventions. Train-only scaling, nested ridge and signed-R2 replacement are changed methods/protocol choices requiring explicit comparison.

metric.description: Primary source code returns per-voxel Pearson r between predicted and observed responses, averaged across the 12 folds. Figure 2 visualizes noise-ceiling-corrected R2. Exact conversion and masks for a published-comparable scalar remain unresolved; signed SSE/SST R2 cannot silently replace correlation-squared.

aggregation.description: Fold mean is source-defined per voxel, with separate participant maps. A single across-voxel/across-participant paper-win scalar, its mask and numerical source baseline have not been recovered. Selecting only favorable voxels or a region after seeing scores is prohibited.

full_panel.description: Retain participants 01, 02 and 03 separately, every original single-trial repetition, all 66 dimensions, every source-eligible voxel and all 12 original session folds. Required outputs comprise original fold-mean Pearson maps and their native permutation companion, Figure 2 noise-ceiling-corrected maps, and the separate Figure 6 joint, unique-dimension, unique-category and shared variance maps with every original ROI summary. Preserve the source shape companion from Supplementary Figure 6/Methods 2. The original masks, numerical maps, ROI identities, shape recipe and applicability of optional face/body-label source branches remain unresolved; this is an unresolved family inventory, not a recovered complete numerical panel. Raw-fMRI preprocessing and the separate time-series/HRF branch are outside this registered single-trial task.

permitted_observations.description: Both information conditions must receive the same versioned paper, original three-participant input/identity manifests and authorized non-code resources. Source 66-dimensional image predictors and original training-fold response estimates may support encoding; held-out responses remain operator scoring-only. Retain the source global feature scaling and separately declare the original variance-partition residualization/label-selection access rather than silently replacing them with train-only or predictive-commonality conventions. Only the verified author-code snapshot is added in paper_data_author_code. No reference maps, private targets, other-condition results or historical solver answers may be added. The full authentic observation/exposure manifests and enforceable participant boundary are absent.

findings.description: Recreate the source article's qualitative finding that behaviour-derived dimensions were superior to categories at predicting brain responses. This is the original comparative scientific claim, not a categorical encoding of map equality. Its supporting participant-specific Figure 6 numerical maps and all original companion analyses remain mandatory, unrepresented numerical outputs under this scalar/categorical schema; this single finding is not a complete reproduction panel.

findings.aggregation: Adjudication must follow the original participant-specific variance-partition maps and reported ROI summaries under source identities; the complete numerical evidence and source-specific inferential rule must be recovered. No newly pooled across-voxel or across-participant statistic is defined.

tolerance.rationale: This is the paper's categorical comparative finding. It supplies no tolerance for required numerical maps or ROI quantities; those remain unresolved and cannot be replaced by category agreement.

uncertainty.method: Recover the source-specific evidential/inferential rule for the dimension-versus-category conclusion and its complete numerical companion panel before assigning a reproduction criterion.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Participant for between-person inference; repeated sessions/stimuli within each original participant for conditional analyses. Voxels and overlapping CV folds are not independent participants.
uncertainty.rationale: The published qualitative statement is known from the permitted paper. Repeating it does not establish computation, evidence of its direction, numerical magnitude or uncertainty; no p-value cutoff, posterior threshold, confidence level or independent-unit minimum is invented.

The required original participant-specific voxel/ROI maps cannot be represented by the current scalar/categorical finding schema. Only the actual source qualitative comparison is represented below. Full_panel and the external interface inventory retain every numerical output family; this partial contract must not be promoted to complete-panel eligibility or treat qualitative agreement as a substitute for those arrays. A source-driven structured-output schema change requires separate review.

Separate from the schema limitation, original per-voxel/ROI numeric results and the complete mask/ROI identity census are unrecovered; no array shape, numerical target, scalar reduction or element enumeration is invented.

The accepted source-session scorer consumes held-out predictions and reports all per-fold/per-voxel r values, but it does not execute or authenticate submitted analyses, source OLS fitting, source permutations, Figure 2 noise-ceiling conversion, Figure 6 residualized attribution or the shape analysis.

No independently justified numerical tolerance or source-specific uncertainty rule is frozen; printed paper values, matching claims or generated source-function parity cannot count as executed reproduction.

Common authentic input manifests, observation/exposure policy, protected candidate execution, cumulative access/compute budgets and separate paper_data/paper_data_author_code runs are unbound.
